iut_type: End Product — BR/EDR+BLE using Combine Unmodified Design
customer_question: How many RF test items are required? Is the RF test scope different for a BR/EDR-only product vs a BR/EDR/LE product? Does using Combine Unmodified Design exempt us from the profile test?
question_variants: Does registering as BR/EDR/LE mean we need more RF test items than BR/EDR-only?
Is the RF Classic test always 26 items?
Does Combine Unmodified Design eliminate the profile test requirement?
actual_issue: Customer needed clarification on: (1) whether RF (Classic Bluetooth) test item count changes based on whether BLE is included; (2) whether Combine Unmodified Design exempts the project from profile PTS testing.
plain_english_explanation: The Classic Bluetooth RF test always consists of 26 fixed items regardless of whether BLE is part of the qualification — the 26 items are all BR/EDR radio parameters. Combine Unmodified Design is exempt from profile PTS testing because the design reuses an existing certified design without modification — the profile tests were already passed as part of the original certification.
consultant_answer: Classic RF test is always 26 items regardless of BLE inclusion. Combine Unmodified Design is exempt from profile PTS testing. Estimated lead times for this project: RF test ~3 days, RF PHY test ~1-15 days (if needed), registration ~3 days after RF test completion.
decision_logic: The 26-item Classic RF test set is fixed by SIG test specifications and does not change based on BLE scope. Profile test exemption under Combine Unmodified Design is explicit SIG policy — when no modifications are made to the pre-certified design, no re-testing is required.
final_recommendation: Always quote Classic RF as 26 items. When using Combine Unmodified Design, inform customers that PTS profile test is not required — this significantly reduces cost and timeline compared to a fresh registration.
risk_if_done_wrong: Incorrectly quoting fewer than 26 RF items would produce an underpowered test scope. Failing to apply the Combine Unmodified Design profile test exemption would over-scope and over-charge the customer.
